import AppKit

/// What the timeline's action lane and the Clip tab's lane share (spec §11
/// CI-4): the ORDER actions are numbered in, the words a band's label is made
/// of, the zoom test, and the one painter both call — so a band on the
/// timeline and the same band in the inspector cannot disagree about its
/// number or its ink.
///
/// Drawn in a FLIPPED view: `minY` is the band's top. Everything here is
/// relative to the band it is handed; where the band sits is its caller's.
enum ActionBands {
    /// Time order — start, then id for two that share one (they cannot
    /// overlap, but a zero-length action can sit on another's start). An
    /// action's NUMBER is its index here plus one, everywhere.
    static func ordered(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> [ActionSnapshot] {
        clip.actions.sorted { ($0.start, $0.id) < ($1.start, $1.id) }
    }

    /// Which properties an action changes — the end patch's keys, spelled
    /// the way the model spells them, sorted (what the old Actions table
    /// printed beside each curve); `speed` when the end names a rate (spec
    /// §11 SR-21 (d)).
    static func keys(of patch: ActionPatch) -> [String] {
        var keys: [String] = []
        if let video = patch.video { keys.append(contentsOf: video.dictionary.keys) }
        if let audio = patch.audio { keys.append(contentsOf: audio.dictionary.keys) }
        if let text = patch.text { keys.append(contentsOf: text.dictionary.keys) }
        if let graphic = patch.graphic { keys.append(contentsOf: graphic.props.keys) }
        if patch.speed != nil { keys.append("speed") }
        return keys.sorted()
    }

    /// A screencast zoom's shape — `add_zoom_action` writes exactly `scale`,
    /// `x` and `y` and nothing else, so an end patch of those three keys is
    /// drawn with the zoom glyph whichever door wrote it. An end naming a rate
    /// is not a zoom (spec §11 SR-21 (d)).
    static func isZoom(_ action: ActionSnapshot) -> Bool {
        let end = action.end
        guard let video = end.video, end.audio?.isEmpty ?? true, end.text?.isEmpty ?? true,
              end.graphic?.props.isEmpty ?? true, end.speed == nil
------
        // what each member means, which is why the per-member descriptions
        // this hand-written property used to carry are not missed: a
        // region's members are part of a VALUE, not arguments of the op.
        let zoomRegionDescription =
            "The rectangle to zoom to, in SOURCE pixels: x and y are its "
            + "CENTRE measured from the centre of the clip's cropped rect — the frame "
            + "video.spotlight and video.obscure use — and width and height its size. "
            + "null is a zoom BACK to the clip's own scale and position; the key is "
            + "required so a forgotten rectangle cannot become that by accident."
        return [

            // MARK: Actions

            opTool(
                "add_action",
                "Adds an animation span to a clip: over `duration` starting at `at`, the clip's "
                    + "properties ease from whatever they are to the span's END state. The end "
                    + "state starts EMPTY — nothing changes until set_action_end fills it in. "
                    + "`at` is CLIP time, measured from the clip's own start, not the "
                    + "timeline's. Refused when it would overlap another action or run past the "
                    + "clip's end. The new action's id comes back as new_actions.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "at": "Where the animation starts, in CLIP time, \(ticks)",
                    "duration": "How long it runs \(ticks) Default 1 s (600000).",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "add_zoom_action",
                "Adds an animation that zooms the picture to a rectangle — the screencast "
                    + "zoom, and what the canvas's Z mode and the Zoom to Region button in "
                    + "the Clip tab's action lane both send. Over `duration` starting at `at`, the clip's scale, x and y "
                    + "ease to the values that bring `region` to the canvas: `fit` shows the "
                    + "whole region, `fill` covers the whole canvas, both measured THROUGH the "
                    + "clip's rotation. `region: null` is a zoom BACK — the end state is the "
                    + "clip's own base scale, x and y. `at` is CLIP time, measured from the "
                    + "clip's own start. Rotation and crop are read from the clip as it is at "
----
                    + "end and later than it ended before, so an action already running past "
                    + "the clip's end (a trim can leave one there) can still be re-curved, "
                    + "moved earlier or shortened. When the action's end names a speed, the "
                    + "change moves how much source the clip reads, and one that would read "
                    + "past the end of its media is refused, naming the latest clip end that "
                    + "fits. "
                    + "Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are "
                    + "re-timed with it in the same step: captions_retimed lists them, and "
                    + "captions_removed those whose speech it no longer plays.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "action": "Action id (get_project lists each clip's actions).",
                    "start": "New start in CLIP time, \(ticks)",
                    "duration": "New length, \(ticks)",
                    "curve": "How the values ease from start to end.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "set_action_end",
                "Sets what an action animates TO. The patch is the action's end state and MERGES "
                    + "into it key by key at every depth (a one-key shadow keeps the rest of it); "
                    + "a key set to null is REMOVED from the end state, so that property stops "
                    + "being animated. Groups are video, audio and text, with the same keys as "
                    + "set_video / set_audio / set_text — a colour is FOUR numbers here too, and "
                    + "it ramps in OKLab with straight alpha, as a graphic colour does; "
                    + "video.chroma.key's three numbers do too. A "
                    + "bad key or value is refused by its path with the group in it "
                    + "(video.filters[1].kind), though values are NOT range-checked: an animation "
                    + "may aim past what a stored property could hold. These keys are refused: "
                    + "video.motion, a preset anchored to the clip's two ends rather than a value "
                    + "to ramp between (set it with set_video), text.words, whose times belong "
                    + "to speech, and video.cutout.subject and video.cutout.quality, the clip's "
                    + "own (set them with set_video; a cutout's edge, feather and background "
                    + "animate). In audio, every key the sound's effects read animates — pan, "
                    + "mono, channels, eq, hum, noise_reduction, gate, leveller, de_esser, "
                    + "compressor, limiter and isolation, beside volume and the fades: numbers "
                    + "ramp, and a "
                    + "switch (a group or an EQ slot turned on, mono, channels, an EQ slope, "
                    + "hum's frequency and harmonics, the leveller's response) changes when the "
                    + "action ENDS; isolation "
                    + "ramps from 0 on a clip with none. duck, keep_pitch, the fade shapes and "
                    + "voice are stored but never animate. "
                    + "A GRAPHIC clip's props are a fourth group, graphic: {props: "
                    + "{<key>: <value>}}, keyed by its module's schema and checked as set_graphic "
                    + "checks them, min and max included, against the module as graphics/ holds it "
                    + "NOW; the app reads that schema, so never send one. A number and a colour "
                    + "ramp along the curve: a number arrives with decimals (64 to 129 is 96.5 "
                    + "halfway), so a module that needs a whole number rounds it, and a colour "
                    + "blends in OKLab, as interpolateColors does, with straight alpha. A string, "
                    + "a boolean and an enum switch to the end's value when the action ENDS. An "
                    + "image (asset) prop switches to the end's image when the action ENDS; \"\" "
                    + "names no image there (null removes the prop from the end). A prop its "
                    + "module marks animate: false is refused: set it with set_graphic. A prop the clip "
                    + "holds no value for starts from the module's current default, written into "
                    + "the clip in the same undo step. "
                    + "graphic.props.<key>: null removes that prop from the end, "
                    + "graphic: null the whole group. get_project shows kinds beside props; the "
                    + "app writes it and ignores one you send, so an end read back can be sent "
                    + "again. While the module is missing or does not compile a prop value is "
                    + "refused (needs its module's schema) — get_graphic says why — and a null "
                    + "still removes. speed, a number beside the groups, is a MEDIA clip's rate "
                    + "(×0.1–×1000, clamped): the clip ramps from the rate in force to it along "
                    + "the curve and holds it after; the clip keeps its start and length and "
                    + "plays more or less source, and an end rate that would read past the end "
                    + "of its media is refused, naming the largest end rate that fits. speed: "
                    + "null removes it. Above ×12 the clip's audio is left out, and the answer "
                    + "carries audio_left_out and audio_note. With speed in the patch, "
                    + "captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are "
                    + "re-timed with it in the same step: captions_retimed lists them, and "
                    + "captions_removed those whose speech it no longer plays.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "action": "Action id.",
                    "patch": "{video?: {...}, audio?: {...}, text?: {...}, graphic?: {props: "
                        + "{...}}, speed?: number} — the properties the animation ends at.",
                    "off": "\"group.key\" paths (video.shadow, text.width, audio.limiter) to "
                        + "switch OFF at the end — stored as null, where a null in patch removes. "
                        + "Optional keys only; never graphic, and never video.cutout (set_video "
                        + "{cutout: null} removes a cutout). One deeper path: "
                        + "audio.eq.<slot> (high_pass, low_shelf, band_1, band_2, band_3, "
                        + "high_shelf, low_pass) switches that EQ slot off at the end.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "remove_action",
                "Removes an animation span. The clip keeps its base properties. Removing one "
                    + "whose end names a speed is refused when the clip would then read past the "
                    + "end of its media, naming the latest clip end that fits. "
                    + "Captions on a Captions track wholly inside a clip with sound are "
                    + "re-timed with it in the same step: captions_retimed lists them, and "
                    + "captions_removed those whose speech it no longer plays.",
                ["clip": clipDescription, "action": "Action id."]),
        ]
    }
}

## Edit the end state

<Steps>

1. [Select the action](/motion/select-an-action/). Clicking its band also moves the playhead to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing.

2. Change any row in the Clip tab. Type a value, drag a slider, pick from a pop-up or choose a colour.

3. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the clip travel to what you set.

</Steps>

While an action is selected, every field shows the value the clip reaches at the action's end, and every edit writes that value. Changing a row adds it to the action, and the row gets a ◆.

Your edits follow the selected action, not the playhead. If the playhead wanders out of the action's span, the action stays selected and the fields keep showing its end. If it moves into another action's span on the clip, that action becomes the selected one.

To edit the clip itself again, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> or click the **Clip** chip at the start of the action lane.

What happens along the way depends on the kind of value. Numbers and most colours ramp along the action's curve, and switches, pop-ups and text hold and then change at the end. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).

## Edit on the canvas

With an action selected, the canvas writes the end state too. Moving, scaling, rotating or cropping the clip, nudging it with the arrow keys, dragging a text clip's wrap width and dragging an obscure region all change that action's end, not the clip.

The box on screen still shows the frame at the playhead, while a drag starts from the end state and changes it by the distance you drag. With the playhead partway through the action, the box moves only part of the way. Work with the playhead at the action's end, which is where clicking the band puts it, and the box lands where you let go.

Two things on the canvas always edit the clip itself:

- A drag on a multi-clip selection. Only a single selected clip can have a selected action.
- Resizing a shape's box, or dragging a line's or arrow's end points. A shape's own properties can't animate. Moving a shape still writes the action's end.

## Switch a property off

Untick a switch inside an action and that property turns off when the action ends. **Drop shadow**, a text clip's **Outline** and **Backdrop**, and sound switches such as **Limit peaks** all work this way, and so does a single band of the EQ.

The property stays on through the action, then goes off as it ends. The row shows ◆ and "at end".

This is different from [taking the row out of the action](#take-a-property-out-of-the-action), which stops the action changing the property at all.

## Read the row marks

Each row in the Clip tab has a narrow gutter to the left of its label. The mark there says how the row relates to the selected action.

| Mark | What it means | How else you can tell |
| --- | --- | --- |

An action shows up in two places: as a band on its clip in the timeline, and as a band in the action lane at the top of the Clip tab. Both are numbered the same way, and you can click or drag a band in either.

At the top of the Clip tab the action lane reads Actions 1, editing 1, with a solid band numbered 1 in the lane beside the Clip chip, and below it the detail row with 00:00:01:00, 2.00 s, Linear and a trash button. On the timeline the same band sits under the clip's name strip, a wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler."
/>

## Bands on the timeline

A clip that has an action shows a lane directly under its name strip, with one band per action. Each band spans the action's time on the clip, and is at least 2 pt wide however short the action is.

Actions are numbered in time order, so a band's number is its place on the clip, and moving an action past another changes both numbers. The number is the same on the timeline and in the Clip tab.

Click a band to select the clip and that action. The playhead moves to the action's end, so the preview shows the state you're editing. Drag a band's body to move the action, or a grip to resize it. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/) and [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).

The selected action's band is solid. A wash runs down the clip under its span, and the span is shaded on the ruler.

A band on a locked track doesn't respond. It doesn't highlight, and clicking it selects the clip, not the action.

### Band detail by track height

How much a band shows depends on [**View ▸ Timeline Track Height**](/timeline/track-height/).
